name: The Palace of the Hour
stub_label: Keep vigil  (rest — the light here does not falter)

plaques.text:
THE PALACE OF THE HOUR

Here the morning was kept before it was rung: twelve offices, one gate, one bell that never came.

The house is awake. Walk as a debt walks — quickly, and owing.

THE BELLMAN'S ECHO

The mother bell remembers the day better than any plaque. ASK her, and she will sing a phrase of it — watch which offices take her light.

Answer the phrase back, office by office, in her order. She does not repeat herself kindly, but she will always sing again.

THE UNLIT PROCESSION

Six keepers' stands walk a ring in the vault. Fire is not obedient here: carry the flame to any stand and its NEIGHBOURS take the change as well — lit gutters, dark kindles, three at every stroke.

The wing rests when the whole procession burns. Walk it with intent; an idle touch digs a hole your reason must climb out of.

THE HOUR GATE

Two rites unbar it: the day rung true, the watch lit whole.

Beyond, the Hour itself is kept. Nothing in this house wants you past this door.

THE ANTECHAMBER

A throne of light, empty. A floor swept for a duel no servant will name.

Whoever keeps the Hour has not forgotten you are coming.

THE BELL-STAIR

Down, and down, and out by the Offices — the short way the ringers kept.

params.notice: Far off, the Hour Gate grinds its bars open.
